current_example.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Interpret the stability of the $x$-axis, the $y$-axis, and the equilibrium point (the origin) for the given decoupled system of linear differential equations.
current_example.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/7500e6aeee318aa22d51d121648ab0e39b0538b0b26a45cf9be052b2b5ce6a6e.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/edda9e7ac817ae01aeeb82d0c8ff575faef9b514e7ee23bbaf45fb3b477ec7a5.svg)

Recall that a homogeneous system of linear differential equations has a single equilibrium (fixed point) at the origin.

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

- Eigenvalue $\lambda_1=2$ with the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/b5d757d3e6fed727f8f1cf20cfb6760efd14297438f9c7314ed9c89fe722570e.svg) The corresponding straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/af18ddb76c1a14950884d24824e48e9214b9850a2dc52b1c0b7ee4ad660d89af.svg)
lie on the $x$-axis and move away from the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, the $x$-axis is the $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{unstable}}$ line.

- Eigenvalue $\lambda_2=4$ with the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/56af2ccd0d92c658ef590c15a729d615e403e2242b8bf81c48714ddc0fa7aedc.svg) The corresponding straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/f60932961bf6a210e36eee29359c3c71c42485ad63e3d12df52964a66253387c.svg)
lie on the $y$-axis and also move away from the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, the $y$-axis is the $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{unstable}}$ line.

Therefore, the equilibrium point (origin) is $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{an unstable node (source)}}.$ 

**Note:** The phase portrait of the system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/2b79201d15fe5d2a9896cdee09c0474b97bb933d75fcf478c6fdb37cb4d16742.png)
